2 ” to allow audio playback Hallo learner, welcome to Science and Technology lesson for Grade 4. Welcome to Science and Technology lesson for Grade 4. Today we are going to learn how to make sinkers float. Welcome to the programme. *Music* We have three states of matter. Which are solids, liquids and gases . When we looked at solids we see that some solids float while other solids sink in water. Before we begin listen to this poem. Sinkers and floaters A plasticine ball sinks, A plasticine boat floats, I know why! The shape of the material. A coin sinks, A leaf floats, I know why! The type of the material. A short pencil floats, A long pencil also floats, I know why! The size of the material. *Music* The poem is about sinkers and floaters. Learner, do you remember what are floaters? And can you name two examples of floaters that you know? *Music* The objects that remain at the surface of water are floaters. The objects that remain at the surface of water are floaters. And examples of floaters include a pencil, a leaf, a paper and many others. Now tell me what are sinkers and name three examples of sinkers. . *Music* Solids that sink in water or they go at the bottom of the water are sinkers. Solids that sink in water or they go at the bottom of the water are sinkers. Sinkers include stones, keys, coins or any other metal and many others. *Music* Learner, can you name some of the factors or reasons that affect floating and sinking. Name factors that affect floating and sinking. *Music*

3 ” to allow audio playback From the poem, we hear that the type of material and shape of the material affects floating and sinking . Learner do you remember a plasticine ball sinks while a plasticine boat floats. Do you know why? Why does a plasticine ball sinks while a plasticine boat floats? *Music* A plasticine ball sinks while a plasticine boat floats because of the shape of the material. The factor that affects the two plasticine items is the shape. The materal is the same; that is plasticine but the different shapes made from the plasticine affect floating and sinking, that is why a plasticine ball sinks while a plasticine boat floats. Let us take another example, a coin sinks while a leaf floats do you know why? Learner, which factor affecting floating and sinking do we notice in a coin and a leaf? *Music* The type of the material makes a coin sink while a leaf floats. The type of the material makes a coin to sink while a leaf to float. Remember materials that sink are called sinkers while those that float are called floaters. Sinkers can be made to float. Sinkers can be made to float. Learner, give me examples of sinkers. *Music* In our poem we take the example of a plasticine ball and a coin, a plasticine ball and a coin. If you look at an example of a plasticine ball which is a sinker then change its shape to be hollow it will float. Learner, can sinkers be made to float? *Music* Yes sinkers can be made to float. A plasticine ball is a sinker and it can be made to float if we change its shape. A plasticine ball is round in shape if we make the shape to be hollow then it will float. Remember when we talked about a ship. Learner does a ship float or sink in water? *Music* A ship even though it is made of metal it floats on water, because a ship has a hollow shape and we can make a ship to float on water because of the shape. Sinkers can be made to float by changing their shape, there are many other ways of making sinkers to float. Learner, can you name other examples of a sinker and how you can make them a floater? Think of other examples of sinkers and how you can make them to be floaters. *Music* Learner, for your task or activity at home, I want you to find other sinkers and different ways they can be made to float. Find other sinkers and ways they can be made to float. With that we have come to the end of our Science and Technology lesson today. Goodbye.
